title: AI service: the AI model is decrypted block by block, and given back after a print without a restart (optional, runs inside the service)
note: OPTIONAL. Install with: --with algo-app-stream-decrypt. When a print reaches its second layer the AI service loads its 44.6 MB encrypted model: QIDI's method reads it whole, decrypts it into a second copy, removes the padding into a third copy and only then writes the temporary file the model is loaded from, so for a moment the service holds about 134 MB more than it needs (from the code; not measured on the printer yet). This module adds one folder to OpenCV's package inside the AI service (_internal/cv2/q2stream/); OpenCV's loader imports it at the end of 'import cv2', and it replaces that one method (after QIDI's module has been imported) by one that reads, decrypts and writes 1 MiB at a time: same key, same cipher, same file, same result byte for byte, a peak of a few MB. It only replaces the method when it still looks exactly like the one it was written for (otherwise a warning in the log and nothing changes), and if anything goes wrong in the new method QIDI's own method does the job. No file of QIDI's or OpenCV's is edited, no key or model is stored in this project, and 'main' stays the original. Log lines in /var/log/algo_app/app_*.log: 'q2stream: DetectionDeal.decrypt_weight now decrypts ...' when the service starts and 'q2stream: model decrypted in N block(s) ...' each time the model is loaded in a print. Second part (separate switch): QIDI's service loads the noodle model in a print's second layer and never lets go of it (its own detector_release() is never called), so it keeps ~100 MB until the service restarts. A small watcher thread per service object calls that QIDI method after the printer has been idle (not printing, not paused, not starting a print; checked again right before) for 120 seconds, then runs the garbage collector and asks glibc to hand the memory back; the next print loads the model again. If the printer object does not look as expected it never releases, and after 5 failed releases it stops trying. The foreign-object model is left alone. Log: 'q2stream: noodle model released after the print (process memory A -> B MB)'. Off switches (systemd environment, each alone): Q2_STREAM_DECRYPT=off for the block-by-block decryption, Q2_STREAM_RELEASE=off for the release; both off leaves everything as it was. Takes effect when the AI service restarts (the installer does that). The block-by-block part does not lower the memory the service uses during the print (the model is still loaded once per print); it removes the short peak at its start. The release part replaces the restart that algo-app-recycle does after a print (the two can be installed together: whichever looks first wins). Uninstall removes the file; an empty folder cv2/q2stream/__pycache__ may stay behind and does nothing. Not installed or measured on the printer yet.
